name: Lords of the Underground
hook: A Newark trio who met at college and brought Marley Marl back into the centre of New York rap in 1993.
blurb: Mr. Funke and DoItAll from Newark, New Jersey, and DJ Lord Jazz from Cleveland met while they were students at Shaw University in North Carolina. A friend introduced them to Marley Marl, who invited them to record at his studio, the House of Hits. Their 1993 album Here Come the Lords is a late Marley Marl production, made after his Juice Crew peak, and it passes his method to the next producer: Marl produced most of it, alone or with his student K-Def, and K-Def produced five or six tracks on his own, including 'Chief Rocka'. One track samples Marl's own 1985 record, 'Marley Marl Scratch', folding the producer's old work back into the new. It had five singles in the charts, including 'Chief Rocka' and 'Funky Child'.

signatureTracks.title: Funky Child
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: One of the album's singles. Its production credit depends on the source: Marley Marl with K-Def, or K-Def alone.

signatureTracks.title: Chief Rocka
